name: Amic Forging Limited
identity_note: Legal name and security checked in cited issuer/exchange filing.
summary: Amic Forging is an industrial forging and precision-machining expansion thesis, not yet an evidence-backed cash compounder. Customer qualification and a real manufacturing history are strengths, and normalized operating earnings improved sharply in FY 26. The decisive weakness is that three years of profits produced little operating cash while capital commitments, financial investments and dilution expanded. At the 19 October 2026 close of ₹2,251.90, the conditional financed base gives ₹1,663.06 terminal value and −5.88% annual return over five years, below the 15% hurdle. BQS is 5.5, GQS 5.0 after the persistent-cash-conversion cap, and IAS 3.0. Classification: weak setup/value-trap risk at this price. Verified commissioning, much better collections and a substantially less demanding entry valuation would change the assessment. This is neither a fraud allegation nor a trade instruction. [S1, RHP, PRESS, APR, JUL, M1]

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Amic Forging Limited, BSE SME code 544037, ISIN INE 0 P 9 J 01013; research cutoff 20 October 2026. The secondary dated close is ₹2,251.90 on 19 October, not a live executable quote. Issued shares are 11,575,035 after primary April/July allotments, giving market capitalization ₹2,606.58 crore; potential shares on all remaining warrant exercises are 13,062,935, with matching unreceived cash addressed separately. The official interoperability master still carries the March share count and is not used for current capitalization. Consolidated accounts use Accounting Standards under section 133, not an assumed Ind AS framework. Units are ₹ crore unless stated otherwise. Horizon is five years to 19 October 2031; nominal INR equity hurdle 15%, before investor taxes; liquidity reference ₹5 lakh, not a recommended allocation. [S1, APR, JUL, SEC, M1]

All four gates are Conditional. G 1: related lending, remuneration and CFO succession require scrutiny, but reviewed records do not establish severe diversion or minority abuse. G 2: signed annual totals, normalization and capital receipts support Medium-confidence modeling; revised-report scope, copied interim rows and a ₹0.30 crore cash-flow arithmetic gap remain explicit bounded caveats. G 3: known financing materially supports projects, while unsanctioned future debt and adverse-case equity are assumptions, not commitments. G 4: a complete secondary trading sample and verified lot support a conditional implementation score, not BSE surveillance clearance or live depth. [S1, REVISION, RES, CFO, APR, JUL, M1, SEC]

Confidence is Medium on historical financials, governance, growth decomposition, capital returns and dated valuation inputs. The weaker confidence concerns source scope and bounded estimation, not a claim that the forecast is likely to occur. No current order-book bridge, engineered remaining-capex certificate or full BSE restriction review is available. Those gaps constrain conclusions; they are not filled with neutral scores or misconduct claims.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 6, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 3, BAL 6, EXEC 5 and EARN 6. IAS factors are R 1, D 2, P 2 and L 7. Each factor has evidence IDs and source-linked reasoning in the factor audit. REV starts at 9 from the preferred five-year CAGR, then the Medium-confidence ceiling limits it to 8; no extra bonus is awarded for announced capacity. CASH 3 reflects several years of poor realization after normalization, not merely one growth-capex year.

BQS contributions are 1.00 +1.20 +0.96 +0.60 +0.60 +0.30 +0.48 +0.40 =5.54, displayed 5.5. GQS contributions are 3.20 +1.20 +0.90 +0.75 +0.30 =6.35 raw; the explicit persistent poor-cash-realization override caps final GQS at 5.00. IAS is 0.25×5.54 +0.35×1 +0.20×2 +0.10×2 +0.10×7 =3.035, displayed 3.0. Coverage is 100% of each original formula, with no redistribution or unsupported midpoint. No governance or funding-failure numeric override is applied.

Judgment sensitivity matters more than a small ranking gap. Moving GOV and CAP together by one point changes BQS by 0.32 and IAS by 0.08, while GQS remains capped at 5 unless the persistent cash weakness itself changes. Moving L by one point changes IAS by 0.10. These variations do not move the record out of the weak-setup classification. Forecast uncertainty remains far wider than the displayed score precision.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Amic manufactures steel forgings and machined heavy precision components for heavy engineering, energy, steel, oil and gas, petrochemicals, power and other industrial applications. The economic service is more than selling steel: forming, metallurgy, heat treatment, machining, testing and delivery to customer specifications create value. The prospectus explains customer prequalification and the cost/time required to secure and retain approved status. Revenue comes from product supply, while working capital is needed before collection. A reputed end market does not make each order recurring or guarantee pricing power. [RHP]

Historical prospectus production rose from 3,961 tonnes in FY 21 to 8,991 in FY 22 and 10,695 in FY 23. Installed capacity rose from 6,300 to 12,600 tonnes, and utilization from 62.87% to 84.88%. These are actual historical disclosures, distinct from the May 2026 capacity plan. That plan describes forging capacity rising from 18,000 to 40,000 MTPA, machining from 8,400 to 33,000 and new ingot capacity 48,000. These are sequential production stages and must not be added into a fictitious 121,000-ton finished-output total. Current achieved output and commercial utilization of the expansion are not independently verified. [RHP, PRESS]

The group includes Amic Engg Tech Private Limited and a 33% interest in Dakor Logistics LLP, which is engaged in warehouse activity. Their economics are not automatically equivalent to forging. The subsidiary's reported loss is immaterial; the associate's ₹4.65 crore carrying value and zero share of profit are kept outside the operating earnings multiple. Quoted securities and financial loans are also valued separately rather than used to inflate the factory margin. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The credible moat mechanism is qualification and process know-how: a customer must evaluate technical specifications, reliability and production capability before accepting a supplier, making switching slower than buying undifferentiated spot steel. Historical capacity utilization and improving core margins are supportive evidence. The durability test is whether Amic retains qualifications and earns cash returns after the entire new plant and working-capital base are funded. The failure mode is a capable competing forge qualifying, customer dual-sourcing, mix reversal or underutilized new equipment. No current independently verified market-share denominator establishes a top-three economic franchise. [RHP, S1]

Three operating comparators challenge the thesis. Bharat Forge's FY 26 primary report shows a much broader automotive/industrial platform, standalone revenue ₹8,395.7 crore, EBITDA ₹2,312.1 crore and net-of-cash ROCE 14.9%; its scale, product breadth and research resources are not a transferable valuation premium. Ramkrishna Forgings describes multiple press, hammer, ring-rolling and warm-forging technologies, with a different component-weight/product mix. CHW Forge describes open-die hydraulic forging, ring rolling, heat treatment and machining, making it a relevant capability competitor but not a listed-multiple comparator. [BFL, RKFL, CHW]

The comparison supports a useful but contestable process advantage, hence MOAT 6 rather than a structural-monopoly score. A refreshed three-company market-multiple table was not established, so no peer P/E is borrowed to justify the terminal multiple. The prospectus flags top-customer dependence; a current quantified concentration/backlog bridge was not located. That is an exposure to monitor, not proof that the customers are connected or that revenue is fictitious. [RHP]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
FY 21–26 reported revenues are ₹26.4088, ₹71.1197, ₹115.8541, ₹126.1467, ₹121.3158 and ₹141.7848 crore. The five-year CAGR is 39.95%; the three-year CAGR from FY 23 is 6.96%. Annual absolute additions are ₹44.7109, ₹44.7344, ₹10.2926, −₹4.8309 and ₹20.4690 crore. Thus the long-term scaling is real, but recent growth is much less rapid than the five-year headline. FY 25 declined 3.83% and FY 26 rose 16.87%. A ten-year comparable audited series is not available in the reviewed set. [RHP, H24, H25, S1]

Pre-IPO restated and subsequent statutory earnings are not silently spliced. FY 23 restated PAT₹9.8001 crore differs from later statutory₹9.6615 crore; the RHP reconciliation includes prior-period and tax adjustments, and the later comparator retains a different accounting presentation. Revenue endpoints agree and the immaterial subsidiary does not explain the growth. The record preserves the original/restated labels rather than treating every small difference as a critical reliability failure. The older history is not penalized simply for a small starting size. [RHP, H24]

Latest comparable H 1/H 2 FY 26 sales were ₹66.5804/₹75.2044 crore, PBT₹16.7091/₹23.0088 crore and pre-NCI PAT₹12.4011/₹15.8681 crore. H 2 is a balancing half-year, not a quarter. Certain owner-PAT/EPS half-year cells appear to repeat annual values; they are not used instead of the signed annual hierarchy. Management's May letter says existing capacity was near full and FY 26 growth was mainly realization/mix-led. That is not independent evidence of volume growth or market-share gain. A numerical current price/volume split remains ND. [RES, REVISION, S1, PRESS]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The opportunity is to move from existing heavy-forging capacity into a larger integrated ingot/forging/machining footprint and then a 5000-ton press with 40-ton manipulator. Management's PhaseI budget is₹150 crore; its June 15,2026 commissioning target remains a target in the sources reviewed. The additional₹165 crore project is called PhaseII in May and PhaseIII in the EGM notice. It is the same project, counted once. Neither a notice nor an authorization proves commercial output, qualified customers or an approved bank loan. [PRESS, EGM]

Base sales are estimated at₹200/280/350/410/470 crore for FY 27–31 and₹520 crore FY 32 run rate. The first capacity expansion's 40,000/18,000 forging ratio is only 2.22 times; applying it mechanically to FY 26 sales gives roughly₹315 crore at unchanged mix/utilization. Therefore₹520 crore requires successful additional heavy-forging capability and/or better value added, not merely PhaseI. The model treats₹520 crore as an explicit analytical supported-capacity assumption, not disclosed engineering output. Beyond that, every₹1.5 crore of added annual revenue capacity requires₹1 crore additional plant investment; the bull and reverse models pay for this rather than assuming unlimited free capacity. [PRESS, EGM; analyst model]

PhaseI remaining cash is estimated at₹50 crore, tested at₹25–80 crore because no current project-wise paid/committed ledger is available. Opening CWIP₹62.4779 crore, capital-goods advances₹7.2903 crore and land advances₹26.3847 crore are not paid twice. Heavy-project future cash₹165 crore is separately scheduled. Operating working capital is 46% of sales in the base, with recurring capex 3.5% and explicit depreciation, financing and dilution. The deferral sensitivity lowers both investment and revenue. [S1; analyst model]

Calculated latest operating ROIC is attractive, but incremental returns on the expanding committed capital base are near the analytical cost-of-capital range and cash realization has been persistently poor. The raw GQS 6.35 is therefore capped at 5.00. Funding activity and a large nominal addressable industry are not evidence that each new rupee compounds at a high return.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The March 2026 disclosure reports promoter holdings 56.56% and no pledge/encumbrance at that date. April/July issuance dilutes percentage ownership if the promoter share count is unchanged; this arithmetic is not a verified current holding statement. Girdhari Lal and Anshul Chamaria remain central to execution. Directors' remuneration rose to₹3.60 crore from₹0.84 crore, about 12.7% of FY 26 owner PAT and 40.6% of reported CFO. The₹2.76 crore increase explains about 82.3% of the₹3.3524 crore increase in employee expense. Consequently, the management narrative of staffing ahead of expansion is not a complete numerical explanation, although factory labor and actual hiring may also have increased. No unsupported claim of unlawful remuneration is made. [S1, OWN, PRESS]

Related Mackeil Ispat & Forgings has a₹2.0358 crore loan balance, disclosed purchases₹2.726 crore, sales₹0.4322 crore, job work₹1.1728 crore and interest₹0.03 crore. The separate₹10.4181 crore OCL Iron & Steel/Samriddhi loan is not labeled related in the note and is not called related by this analysis. Financial lending and the₹11.2849 crore investment book compete for capital with the factory. However the₹32.4353 crore investing-advance increase is mostly land/capital advances, not all lending or alleged diversion. CARO observations describe stipulated repayment and collection efforts; that is not evidence that every balance has already been collected. [S1]

CFO succession is a specific open issue: Anshul ceased the role 1 November 2025; Priyankar Ghosh was appointed 20 December and left 31 March 2026. The 7 April filing attributes resignation to personal reasons and says replacement is in process; the annual report still describes the vacancy. The 20 April director appointment was non-executive Vijay Chopra, not a CFO replacement. A later successor was not verified. K N Gutgutia & Co continues as statutory auditor through the stated 2029 AGM term; the August internal/cost-auditor reappointments are not a statutory-auditor resignation. [CFO, S1]

Promises versus delivery: historical FY 23 output/utilization growth is verified; FY 26 sales and normalized margin improvement are verified; May's June 15 PhaseI target is unverified as achieved; the₹165 crore project remains a financing/execution proposal rather than proven earnings. The July 3 revised audit filing responds to a BSE discrepancy request, but the specific exchange objection is not attached. The report remains unmodified. This warrants precise source hierarchy and follow-up, not a misconduct inference. [RHP, PRESS, EGM, REVISION]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Three-year operating bridge, FY 24/FY 25/FY 26 respectively: revenue₹126.1467/121.3158/141.7848 crore; calculated core EBITDA₹16.4871/27.9978/45.9478 crore; core EBIT₹15.7732/25.1273/42.3561 crore; reported owner PAT₹13.8331/35.5570/28.2716 crore; diluted EPS₹16.06/33.90/26.30; CFO−₹7.9614/₹6.0150/₹8.8593 crore; cash PPE capex₹4.7655/31.9603/63.0460 crore; FCF proxy−₹12.7269/−₹25.9453/−₹54.1867 crore. CFO is consolidated, with FY 26 group PAT₹28.2692 crore before minority for the comparable conversion ratio. It is not mixed with an unrelated standalone cash perimeter. [H24, S1]

Normalization is explicit: FY 26 core EBITDA =PBT 39.7183 +finance 0.4802 +depreciation 3.5917 +investment loss 3.1904 −other income 1.0328 =45.9478. FY 25 other income₹20.7091 crore included investment gains₹18.9477 crore; the reported PAT decline is not a collapse of forging profitability. Core EBITDA margins rose from 13.07% to 23.08% to 32.41%. Normalized operating NOPAT at 25% tax is₹11.8299/18.8455/31.7671 crore, not a claim about exact normalized owner PAT. Historical reported taxes and non-operating income remain in the original accounts. [H24, S1]

FY 24–26 CFO totals₹6.9129 crore against group PAT₹77.6593 crore,8.9%; against normalized operating NOPAT it is 11.1%. Financing-classified cash interest makes owner realization weaker still. Capex explains FCF but does not explain weak CFO: FY 26 receivables absorbed₹25.5381 crore and inventory₹11.6629 crore. Average receivable days using total revenue as a credit-sales proxy rose from 85.1 in FY 25 to 103.5 in FY 26. Receivables₹52.9745 crore include₹50.2412 crore under six months and₹1.3911 crore aged 1–2 years; most are current, but collection has slowed. Inventory is₹27.7624 crore versus₹16.0995 crore, with both raw material and finished stock increasing. Payables₹17.9373 crore partly fund the cycle; they are not an unlimited funding source. [S1]

Committed-capital proxy is equity including warrant money plus debt/NCI minus cash, financial investments and financial loans, retaining CWIP and land/capital advances. It gives approximately₹3.6305 crore FY 23,₹70.8194 crore FY 25 and₹187.8124 crore FY 26. FY 26 NOPAT on average FY 25/26 capital is 24.6%; the FY 23–26 incremental proxy is about 12.0%, and FY 25–26 about 11.0%. FY 23's very small residual denominator reflects supplier funding and financial-asset allocation, so its apparent spot return is not a durable project return. Commissioning lags and mix improvement also prevent attributing all profit change to new investment. Compared with a 12–16% analytical nominal INR capital-cost range, incremental economics remain mixed; this range is separate from the 15% equity hurdle. A fully mapped five-year incremental-capital series is ND. [H24, H25, S1]

March debt is₹5.6365 crore, including₹3.4750 crore current maturities. Reported cash₹6.7736 crore already nets a negative Kotak balance₹2.1699 crore: adding that debt again without grossing cash would double count. Current-tax provision₹11.0904 crore is netted against identified tax assets₹1.7240 crore in the model, outside ordinary WC. The CFS states opening₹19.5301 less net decrease₹13.0565 but closes₹6.7736, leaving₹0.30 crore arithmetic difference. Parent investment₹0.70 crore and minority capital/loss arithmetic make a minority subscription a plausible explanation, not a confirmed missing line. A lower-cash sensitivity is included; the discrepancy is small versus assets and fundraising, and does not overturn the negative valuation conclusion. [S1]

Current claims must use allotments, not stale master capital. March shares 10,748,835 plus April 800,000 plus July 26,200 give 11,575,035. Remaining 65,000 old and 1,422,900 new warrants imply 13,062,935 potential shares and₹170.2322 crore unreceived exercise cash. The base assumes neither future exercise cash nor the corresponding new shares; a matched alternative adds both. Original warrant deposits and March receipts are not added a second time. Contingent claims are reported NIL in the latest annual note, which is not an independent guarantee that no future obligation can arise. [S1, APR, JUL, SEC]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At₹2,251.90 and current issued shares, market value is₹2,606.58 crore, about 92.2 times FY 26 owner PAT. A deliberately dated March-balance operating EV cross-check, subtracting cash, investments and financial loans and adding debt/NCI, is about 56.2 times normalized EBITDA. It is not a current October EV: post-March fundraising and deployment must be bridged. Reported FCF is negative, so a positive owner-FCF yield is not asserted. Book/asset support cannot independently justify the market value, and land, CWIP or investments are not added twice. [M1, S1, APR, JUL]

The linked annual model starts with March balances plus verified incremental April₹55.4345 crore, July equity₹3.9955 crore and July warrant deposits₹54.2481 crore. It retains₹2 crore operating reserve and settles prior-year net tax. Base sales are₹200/280/350/410/470/520 crore annual run rates, margin 30%, tax 25%, WC 46%, remaining PhaseI₹50 crore and heavy-project₹165 crore. Maintenance/growth capex is 3.5% of sales. Debt 11.5% includes half-year new-draw interest solved iteratively; old maturities are paid, debt caps and equity dilution are explicit. The model's funding is conditional, not sanctioned. No dividends are double-counted with retained cash. [S1, APR, JUL, PRESS, EGM; analyst model]

Terminal normalized operating NOPAT is capitalized at 18 times in the base,12 times bear and 22 times bull, then cash and non-operating recoverable assets are added and debt/NCI subtracted. These are analyst normalization ranges, not imported peer P/Es. Base₹1,663.06 gives−5.88% IRR, no material new equity and₹46.24 crore cumulative debt draws, repaid in the later base years. Bear₹333.34 gives−31.76% with₹59.50 crore equity; bull₹3,420.35 gives 8.72% after paying additional capacity capex. Matched warrant exercise gives₹1,609.14 and−6.50% because proceeds and dilution both count. Heavy-project deferral with lower growth gives₹1,385.10 and−9.26%. [Analyst model]

Two-way margin/multiple sensitivity is explicit: at 25% margin, values at 12/18/22 times NOPAT are₹874/1,286/1,561; at 30%,₹1,150/1,663/2,005; at 33%,₹1,313/1,887/2,269. Even the favorable 33%/22 times combination on the base sales path gives only about 0.15% annual return. PhaseI remaining cost₹25–80 crore changes base IRR to roughly−5.43% to−6.48%; WC 55% gives−6.42%, total loan loss−6.04%, and 14% funding rate−5.90%. The conclusion is driven more by the entry expectations than by a tiny accounting or interest adjustment.

At 12%/15%/18% equity hurdles, assumption-dependent base entry values are₹943.67/826.84/726.94. These are not observable fair values or executable orders. A funded reverse model holding 30% margin,46% WC and 18 times terminal NOPAT needs about 70.54% growth after FY 27's₹200 crore to a₹2,884.82 crore FY 32 run rate, with₹1,645.07 crore gross extra equity once beyond-capacity plant is funded. This is a mathematical expectation test, not a credible capacity forecast. The market price requires substantially more than completion of announced PhaseI.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that all profits are false. It is that genuinely improved factory margins attract an excessive valuation before collections and new-capital returns are proven. Customer qualification or demand delays then lower utilization, steel/mix pressure reduces margin, receivables and inventory consume cash, and the larger plant cannot be deferred costlessly. Additional equity preserves operations while diluting existing claims, and the terminal multiple normalizes. [RHP, S1, PRESS, EGM]

The linked bear assumes sales₹160/190/220/250/275/295 crore,23% margin,55% WC,₹80 crore remaining PhaseI spend,₹165 crore heavy-project spend,₹5 crore operating-asset impairment and 50% loan/investment recovery. It requires₹59.50 crore gross equity and produces₹333.34 terminal price, roughly 85.2% below entry. Severe assumptions give about₹34.00,98.5% below entry, with₹56.57 crore equity. These scenarios are not assigned invented probabilities. Permanent-impairment risk at this entry is High, even though March leverage alone is low.

Operating impairments reduce recoverable opening WC and are replenished only through the future required operating stock; they are not fabricated immediate cash payments. Financial-asset haircuts reduce the asset claim and accounting profit, without both deducting a cash payment and retaining the original recoverable balance. The base's large financial reserves are valuable, but do not eliminate valuation loss. The decisive thesis variable is cash return on the expanded capital base, not a single revenue announcement.

The strongest counterevidence is the verified historical production increase, customer qualification and FY 26 core-margin improvement. Successful heavy-forging entry with sustained high margins and better collections could outperform the base. What is not supported is treating commissioning, refinancing, order conversion and premium valuation as simultaneously certain.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold prices from₹2,251.90 are₹11,259.50 and₹22,519.00 over five years. Before any additional dilution these imply roughly₹13,032.91 crore and₹26,065.82 crore equity values. Business sales growth, enterprise value and per-share return are different: capex, WC, debt and new shares must all be funded.

The financed reverse search retains base margins and valuation, funds capacity beyond the named projects at an explicit 1.5 times sales/capital assumption, and tests 0–90% annual sales growth after FY 27. It finds no 5× or 10× per-share solution within that range. This is not a mathematical proof of impossibility under every future business model; it demonstrates that the current thesis needs far more favorable economics than the tested base. Even the bull case gives only about 1.52 times the current price, with 8.72% annual return.

Classification: speculative/unsupported as a 5× or 10× proposition at this entry. A materially cheaper entry, much stronger capital turnover, sustained margins and verified customer absorption could change the arithmetic, but none is awarded in advance. The 15% hurdle reverse solution itself is far beyond currently verified capacity and execution, so it is not presented as a target.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Collections: FY 26 average receivable days 103.5 versus 85.1 in FY 25; require stabilization and cash realization rather than sales growth alone. A further comparable-period rise with weak CFO triggers a full funding/model review. Track the₹1.3911 crore 1–2-year debtor bucket and actual recoveries. [S1]

2. Operating cash: FY 24–26 CFO₹6.91 crore versus₹77.66 crore group PAT. Look for sustained improvement after cash interest, not one release of payables or inventory. Another growth period funded chiefly by fresh equity without improved realization keeps the cash-quality cap. [S1, H24]

3. PhaseI delivery: obtain a dated commercial-commissioning/qualification disclosure, actual output, utilization and a paid/committed project ledger against the₹150 crore budget. The June 15 target alone is not achievement; costs above the modeled₹80 crore remaining-stress level require remapping the funding case. [PRESS, S1]

4. Heavy project: verify₹165 crore scope, financing, orders, delivery and customer qualification. Reconcile PhaseII/III naming to prevent double counting. Any delay must lower revenue assumptions as well as move spending. [EGM, PRESS]

5. Capital claims: track the 65,000 and 1,422,900 warrant tranches, cash receipts, expiration/forfeiture and actual shares. Do not update one side of the conversion bridge without the other. Review preferential proceeds utilization and any new commitments. [APR, JUL, USE]

6. Allocation/governance: monitor Mackeil₹2.0358 crore and OCL/Samriddhi₹10.4181 crore loan recovery, investment exposure, related remuneration and CFO replacement. A substantive adverse audit finding or evidenced abusive transaction changes gate treatment; routine restatements alone do not. [S1, CFO]

7. Operating economics: compare normalized margin against the 30% base and 25% sensitivity, separate price/mix from tonnage, and verify returns including CWIP/advances. Growth beyond the modeled capacity requires explicit extra plant and WC funding. [S1, PRESS]

8. Implementation: before any trade, refresh lot, BSE restrictions, live depth/spread and the 20/60-session sample. One 100-share lot costs₹225,190; two lots₹450,380 and three₹675,570 straddle the₹5 lakh reference. The theoretical turnover test is not an execution guarantee. [M1, SEC]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
BQS 5.54, capped GQS 5.00 and IAS 3.035 place Amic in weak setup/value-trap risk under the framework at the dated price. Displayed scores are 5.5/5.0/3.0. This is an industrial expansion/cyclical-quality thesis with useful manufacturing capabilities, not an evidence-backed compounder designation. No critical gate failure is established, but all gates remain Conditional for the stated reasons.

The price conclusion is negative even when actual issued shares, verified financing receipts and improved operating margins are credited. It is not produced by automatically excluding BSE SMEs, treating a minor cash-flow discrepancy as fraud, or ignoring the financing value of warrant deposits. Conversely, robust recent turnover does not rescue an inadequate prospective return. The model's approximate₹827 entry for a 15% hurdle is highly assumption-dependent, not a personalized buy price.

Action category: research watchlist; wait for evidence of cash returns and a better-supported valuation setup. For an existing holding, this is a valuation, cash-conversion and capital-allocation review candidate, not an automatic sell instruction. Position size, taxes, live trading conditions and the user's portfolio were not supplied. No trade or publication action follows automatically from the analysis.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source ledger links the FY 26, FY 25 and FY 24 audited reports, IPO RHP, April/July allotments, May business update/results, June EGM notice, CFO resignation, July revised audit, March ownership/utilization disclosures and exact dated market sources. Material claims above carry source IDs; factor and calculation evidence is separately typed as verified disclosure, calculation, management statement or analyst assumption. Annual financial pages 94–97 and notes 10–17/19/24/25 are the key financial locators. The full annual model preserves year-by-year debt, equity, capex, WC, cash and terminal bridges.

Open questions with economic consequences: the latest achieved capacity and customer qualification; remaining paid/committed PhaseI and heavy-project costs; current order/customer concentration; CFO successor; actual loan recoveries; the exact₹0.30 crore CFS bridge; the specific exchange request behind the revised audit; future warrant exercise; current BSE restrictions and live depth. None is silently declared resolved. The small cash arithmetic issue is bounded in a sensitivity, whereas uncertain project costs and utilization are treated through substantial scenario ranges.

The known FY 26 statements are not a current October cash balance. No unreceived warrant cash is assumed in the no-exercise base, no capital advance is paid twice, no announced tonnage stages are summed, no quoted investment gain is capitalized as recurring forging profit, and no financial-asset write-off is invented as a second immediate cash outflow. The primary peer material supports operating comparison, not a refreshed listed-peer multiple valuation. The 15% hurdle, terminal multiples, economic useful lives, future debt capacity, equity discount and expansion asset turns are disclosed analytical assumptions. Medium evidence confidence does not mean narrow forecast risk.

valuation.status: Conditional financed annual model; analyst estimates, not committed financing or verified commissioning
assumption_basis: All monetary values are INR crore except per-share prices. The March 2026 balance sheet is bridged with verified April and July cash receipts; FY 27 is a full-year estimate including the elapsed period, not a reported October balance sheet. The terminal date is 19 October 2031, exactly five years after the dated price. FY 32 contributes only the 202-day stub cash flow; the terminal operating run rate is annualized separately.

Current issued shares are 1.1575035 crore. The base assumes no additional warrant exercise or unreceived exercise cash. A matched alternative adds 0.14879 crore shares and INR 170.2321875 crore cash in FY 28. The warrants expire on their contractual terms; this sensitivity is not a forecast of exercise. Equity to fund other deficits is issued at 30% below the entry price with 5% issue costs, and is not assumed to be available with certainty.

April proceeds are only INR 55.4344938 crore: the initial 25% deposit and INR 17.2255 crore of subsequent receipts were already in the March accounts. July adds INR 3.9955 crore equity proceeds and INR 54.2480625 crore warrant deposits. Counting the entire April conversion consideration again would overstate cash.

Opening reported cash INR 6.7736 crore already nets the negative Kotak bank balance. The model retains INR 2 crore as an operating reserve and settles INR 11.0904 crore current-tax provision net of INR 1.724 crore related tax assets. This prior-year settlement is separate from forecast current taxes. Earmarked financing remains available for its matching project uses, not excluded and then funded a second time.

Base sales are INR 200,280,350,410,470 and 520 crore for FY 27 through the FY 32 run rate, with 30% operating EBITDA margin, 25% normalized tax and operating working capital at 46% of annual sales. These are scenarios, not guidance. FY 26 revenue was INR 141.7848 crore and calculated core EBITDA margin 32.41%; the terminal sales case requires successful additional heavy-forging capability as well as PhaseI. No verified current order book or project-specific throughput proves this forecast.

PhaseI remaining cash is estimated at INR 50 crore, tested at INR 25–80 crore, because the INR 150 crore budget is not accompanied by a current project-wise paid/committed ledger. It is paid 70% inFY 27 and 30% inFY 28. Existing CWIP and capital-goods advances are commissioned without paying their historical costs again. Land advances are not depreciated or independently added to terminal equity.

The INR 165 crore 5000-ton press/40-ton manipulator project appears as PhaseII in May and PhaseIII in the June EGM. It is counted once, with 55% cash spending inFY 28 and 45% inFY 29. Deferring it is tested with a correspondingly lower revenue path, not free growth without the investment.

Base maintenance and incremental replacement capex is 3.5% of sales; it is separate from the named expansion. New equipment uses 15-year and building 30-year analytical depreciation, with a 70/30 allocation of new project spend. Existing CWIP is split between disclosed building, machinery and office. Terminal normalized depreciation is at least recurring capex, avoiding a perpetually free replacement assumption. These are economic-life estimates, not an engineering appraisal.

New debt is limited by the lower of the scenario rupee cap and two times annual EBITDA, with existing debt preserved where necessary. Interest is 11.5% on opening debt less half-year scheduled repayment plus half-year new draws, solved iteratively. Scheduled old maturities are paid, surplus cash repays debt and residual cash remains in terminal equity. These analytical facilities are not sanctioned loan commitments.

Non-operating loans INR 12.4539 crore earn an assumed 6% interest before tax; the terminal balance and investments INR 11.2849 crore are added only once outside operating enterprise value. Haircuts reduce principal and accounting profit without inventing an immediate cash payment or tax shield. Operating-asset impairment reduces recoverable opening working capital, and replacement funding restores only the required future operating stock.

Terminal values capitalize normalized operating NOPAT at 12,18 and 22 times in bear,base andbull cases, plus cash and non-operating assets less debt and minority claim. These are analyst normalization ranges, not current peer-derived market multiples. No dividends are assumed; retained cash is not counted again as a distribution.

An additional capacity-consistency charge funds sales beyond an assumed INR 520 crore annual capacity supported by the named projects, or INR 315 crore if the heavy-press project is deferred. Each incremental INR 1.5 crore of annual sales capacity requires INR 1 crore of extra plant investment, with depreciation included. These capacity/value-added and asset-turn assumptions are analyst estimates, not disclosed engineered capacities. Beyond-capacity capex is charged fully when first needed, including in the terminal stub; large reverse-growth solutions remain hypothetical even after this charge.
